Spencer Platt/Getty Images Hannah Einbinder has released a statement after being arrested on Thursday during a protest ahead of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ‘s United Nations address. “If the pictures of my friends and me getting arrested in protest of Netanyahu’s shameful visit to New York draw attention to anything, let it be to the devastating genocidal war Israel is waging against people of Palestine and Southern Lebanon-to the settler attacks, the home demolitions, the bombing of people as they sleep; to the crimes that happen every SINGLE day but garner almost no international press coverage,” the actress wrote on her Instagram Story on Thursday. “The US government has the power to bring an end to all of this killing, pillaging, and land theft, yet instead it chooses to welcome the butcher of Gaza with open arms.” Related Stories General News Susan Sarandon, Hannah Einbinder Detained at United Nations Netanyahu Protest News Hannah Einbinder Defends Mark Ruffalo From Paramount "Antisemitism" Claim: "All of Us Artists Could Stand to Be More Like Mark" The Hacks actress, Susan Sarandon and Caleb Hearon were among those reportedly taken into custody alongside around 100 protesters before Netanyahu addressed the United Nations General Assembly. Cynthia Nixon and Sarah Sherman were also at the protest, with Einbinder being photographed with the Saturday Night Live star. Einbinder concluded, “The fact that the orchestrator of all this bloodshed is roaming freely in our cities is an indictment of BOTH REPUBLICANS AND DEMOCRATS who enable and protect architects of genocide like netanyahu [sic]. Let us not mistake the spectacle for the story: genocide is the headline, and it is time for it to end.” In a second Instagram Story, she shared a link to donate to Pal Humanity. A spokesperson for the New York City Police Department told The Guardian that officers responded to “unscheduled demonstration” reports where an intersection was blocked. “Members of the NYPD Community Affairs Bureau issued … warnings, advising participants that they should leave,” the spokesperson told the outlet. “They continued to block the intersection. Multiple individuals who didn’t comply were taken into custody.” The actress-comedian has been a vocal supporter of Palestinian rights. At the end of her acceptance speech for supporting comedy actress at the 2025 Emmys, Einbinder said, “I just wanna say, finally, go birds, fuck ICE and free Palestine.” The Hollywood Reporter reached out to Einbinder’s reps for additional comment, but did not hear back. THR

title: David Ellison, Tech Titans and Fox News Hosts Attend White House State Dinner Honoring China’s President
full_text: × Skip to main content By Alex Weprin Plus Icon Alex Weprin Senior Editor alexweprin Follow Sign Up View All September 24, 2026 6:45pm President of China Xi Jinping clinks glasses with U.S. first lady Melania Trump as U.S. President Donald Trump speaks during a state dinner in the East Room of the White House on September 24, 2026 in Washington, DC. Photo by Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images Tech and media titans… as well as a small army of Fox News hosts descended on the White House Thursday evening to attend the state dinner honoring China’s president Xi Jinping. President Trump and First Lady Melania Trump hosted the dinner, which was heavy on corporate bigwigs. According to a guest list released by the White House, attendees included Paramount Skydance CEO David Ellison , just days after his company inked a settlement to clear its takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery … including CNN, which saw its reporters denied access to the state dinner even after a federal judge reinstated their press passes to the White House complex. But it was mostly tech giants in attendance, with photos showing Tesla and SpaceX chief Elon Musk sitting at the head table with Trump and Xi, joined by Nvidia’s Jensen Huang and Apple’s Tim Cook. Earlier this week, there were reports that Ellison may ask Musk to invest in Paramount as part of its WBD takeover. Other attendees included OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, Amazon’s Jeff Bezos, OpenAI president Greg Brockman, Google co-founder Sergey Brin and CEO Sundar Pichai, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, TikTok investor Jeff Yass, and LCMH CEO Bernard Arnault, along with a slew of other CEOs from finance, manufacturing and other industries. And there was also a Fox News contingent, with hosts Jesse Watters and Laura Ingraham as well as anchor Bret Baier all making the cut too. Podcast hosts, including Katie Miller (the wife of White House aide Stephen Miller) and David Sacks (tech investor and All-In co-host) were on the list, as was Cheryl Hines, who was there with her husband RFK Jr. THR

title: Inside the Hollywood Home Studio That’s Birthed Several Pop Hits
full_text: × Skip to main content By Nicole Fell Plus Icon Nicole Fell Associate Editor nicolemfell Follow Sign Up View All September 24, 2026 6:12pm Leland in his home studio. Courtesy Situated in the hills of Studio City sits a home studio that’s birthed a slew of popular songs. “The first session I did here was with MUNA in 2019,” says Leland . The 39-year-old producer owns that home studio. It’s first iteration was situated inside the main house on his property and has since expanded into its own little oasis. Steeped in warm colors, with luxurious candles burning away, Leland’s current studio feels more like a chic getaway spot rather than a workspace. It’s become a home base for him and other creatives in his circle to collaborate. His dog, Crosby, is a frequent visitor and how he’s keeping track of the passing time — the MUNA session had to be in 2019 because he has a photo of one of the band’s members with the dog as a puppy. Related Stories Music Teyana Taylor, Charli xcx, Belmont Cameli Join 2026 MTV VMAs Presenters Lineup (Exclusive) Music MTV VMAs Producer Van Toffler Promises a "Kick-A**, Fast-Paced Show," Says Madonna's Performance "Will Make Your Head Spin" The actual studio only accounts for, at times, 50 percent of where the creativity’s happening when artist comes to Leland’s place. “The writing doesn’t have to happen in the studio. The recording can happen in the studio,” the producer explains. “I feel like a lot of it is just sitting out here having conversations.” Leland in his home studio. Courtesy An artist might be staying in the cottage on the property while they’re there working. “They can just walk down to the studio, which has been really nice,” says Leland. The Shards star Hayes Warner , another collaborator of Leland’s, stayed in his cottage while she was filming the Ryan Murphy show. Leland wrote music for the series, which is set to release a soundtrack next month . On a day where he’s welcoming an artist into the studio, the producer tends to start the day with a hike. He’ll walk to Fryman — if you ever see someone dangerously walking down Laurel Canyon Boulevard, it’s likely Leland. He’s only had one close call, he points out, and it was actually from a friend. “One of my best friends happened to be driving down Laurel Canyon, and he was like, ‘Girl, did I almost hit you?’ I was like, ‘Yes, but I would’ve wanted it to be a friend,'” he says cheekily. After his hike, hopefully without any close calls, Leland will get fresh flowers for the studio, along with a candle or incense. His routine tends to change depending on who he’s working with that day. “I love getting the studio ready for a session. I love that part of it,” the producer says. “Or cleaning up after a session, which is usually just Goop [Kitchen] bags, water and Coke Zero.” The space is meant to be a space of peace and quiet, even if that’s not always what’s happening in the studio itself. Leland, who’s also RuPaul’s Drag Race ‘s producer and songwriter, explains that it can range from longtime collaborator Troye Sivan to Charli xcx , who he says recorded some of the Wuthering Heights album in the studio, to Demi Lovato. A Drag Race executive producer or even RuPaul might be around while Leland’s tinkering on Sivan’s work, so they’ll share it. Leland in his home studio. Courtesy If Leland’s working with an artist for the first time, he’ll listen to their music on his morning hike — or he’ll listen to anything he’s anticipating will be a good reference point for the work that’ll happen later that day. No matter how familiar with the project or the artist, he wants to be prepared and have something in his back pocket. Some artists, however, have a good idea coming into their sessions with Leland. “When Rebecca Black came in, I was so excited to work with her and she had such a clear vision for what she wanted to make, and it was just so fun,” he says. The pair wrote the track “Corsetry” from her latest album in the space. “I have the same feeling about [Black] that I had when Adéla first walked into the room,” Leland says of the pop princess of the moment. The 22-year-old has been blowing up this summer. Leland and the pop star — who broke out as a contestant on the audition project Dream Academy that formed the girl group KATSEYE — worked together on songs from her first EP, “SexOnTheBeat” and “DeathbyDevotion.” Leland, by his on admission, loves working with women. “I love a pop girl,” he says. But by far, the producer’s most impactful collaboration, both professionally and creatively, remains Sivan. Getting to be part of a gay pop star’s career is something he’ll never take for granted. “So many songs that you love that are by the female pop stars that we love, a lot of the times there’s a queer person as one of the collaborators when you look up the credits,” Leland says. “I think now my ear is trained to where I can tell if a gay person was in the room or not.” He adds, “I really think for songs, you can tell. And not that every song needs to have a gay person in the room, obviously, but I think depending on what you’re going for, you can really hear if there was some queer energy in the room or not. I feel like it’s been so fun to sometimes be that person with the different artists that come through.” Leland in his home studio. Courtesy Leland and Sivan collaborated once again for the pop star’s upcoming album She’s the Best , set to be released next month. Many of the great pop stars of the past weren’t publicly out, so watching Sivan’s career get to the point it’s at now has been almost surreal for Leland. “People like Troye are allowed to be pop stars, and you’re allowed to have that experience, and maybe not allowed, you’re demanding it,” the producer says. “I always want the music to speak for itself. I don’t want opportunities because I’m queer. I want opportunities because I’m good. I don’t want opportunities for Troy because he’s a gay pop star,” says Leland. “I want opportunities for him and for our music because the music is good and the music videos are good and the team’s good and the energy is good.” He adds, “I want that support from the queer community because the music is great and the art is great. I want that support from the straight community because the music is great and the art is great, not just because any of us happen to be queer.” THR

title: ‘Unabomber’ Review: Jacob Tremblay and Russell Crowe in a Facile Rendering of Ted Kaczynski’s College Days
full_text: × Skip to main content By Richard Lawson Plus Icon Richard Lawson View All September 24, 2026 6:00pm Jacob Tremblay in 'Unabomber.' Philippe Bosse/Netflix While Netflix has Ryan Murphy busy investigating (or flat-out making up) the motives of killers like Jeffery Dahmer, the Menendez Brothers and Lizzie Borden, the streamer has enlisted director Janus Metz to tell the story of Ted Kaczynski , the math prodigy turned reclusive murderer known as the Unabomber — also the movie’s title. But Unabomber , written by Sam Chalsen and Nelson Greaves, is not some sweeping birth-to-death survey of Kaczynski’s life. It instead focuses on a young Kaczynski’s time at Harvard University, where he participated in a brutal psychological study that, in the movie’s framing, may have helped form the anarchic worldview that eventually led to his infamous deeds. Related Stories TV Felicia Pride on Capturing Innocence, Humanity in 'A Different World' Sequel and Revering the Original: "We're Not Replacing It" TV Keira Knightley, Ben Whishaw Reunite as Old Killers With New Enemies in 'Black Doves' Season 2 Trailer Never mind that Kaczynski himself has said that the study, conducted by psychology professor and sometime government operative Henry Murray, didn’t have much effect on his life. Unabomber presupposes that it did, that Murray’s cruel (and later condemned) experiment in breaking down the philosophical principles of test subjects, stoked a rage — at academia, at technology, at universities — so fierce that Kaczynski later decided to enact his revenge. Perhaps not figuring that argument compelling enough on its own, the film tacks on a 1990s-set plot covering the days leading up to Kaczynski’s capture in Montana. Unabomber The Bottom Line A faint sketch of a killer as a young man. Release date: Friday, Sept. 25 Cast: Russell Crowe, Jacob Tremblay, Shailene Woodley, Annabelle Wallis, Gus Halper Director: Janus Metz Screenwriters: Sam Chalsen, Nelson Greaves Rated R, 1 hour 37 minutes Both narratives concern people prying into Kaczynski’s psyche and finding only further questions. In the 1950s, in the hallowed, lacquered-wood halls of Harvard, we watch a perspicacious boy genius — Kacyznski was all of 16 when he started college — as his intellect, his curiosity and his naiveté are weaponized against him, hardening his most radical beliefs into ideology. In the 1990s section, we observe relative lay people as they try to divine specific clues from Kaczynski’s manifesto, markers that might give away something crucial. These twin analyses are both facile and unenlightening. The investigation arc is so boilerplate that it has an FBI agent placing a pile of documents on her desk and saying to them, “Talk to me.” The 1950s portion of the film is at least able to conjure up some mid-century moodiness, skulking around in the nervous temper of early Cold War days, as academia colluded with government agencies to buttress the country against the perceived Soviet threat. (At its best, the film calls to mind Robert De Niro’s unfairly maligned CIA origin story The Good Shepherd , which begins its postwar tale on the leafy quads of Yale.) And yet, the ultimate conclusions of that half of the film are just as unpersuasive as everything that happens 40 years later. That’s largely owed to starchy, frequently clichéd writing. But sadly one must put some of the blame on the actor playing Kaczynski, Jacob Tremblay , who long ago escaped the confines of Room and now, at 19, has found himself in this dark mess. His clean-cut boyish features do actually resemble Kaczynski at that age, but Tremblay otherwise has trouble evoking the volatile storms of Kaczynski’s mind. His voice cracking and eyes wide with alarm, Tremblay effectively communicates Kaczynski’s youth, but it all plays as bratty and insouciant rather than registering as the beginnings of true menace. Tremblay was a better fit for his other recent film about extremism, 2025’s Sovereign , in which his guilelessness served a more poignant purpose. As Murray, Russell Crowe has dusted off his A Beautiful Mind professorial duds and phones in a performance of avuncular appeal masking sinister motives. We believe that Murray cares, in some way, for Kazcynski — or, at least, that he’s impressed by the student’s prowess — but not enough to stop his predatory work. The portraiture is not very detailed beyond that. Part of the problem may be that, for the bulk of the experimentation, Murray is out of the room. Kaczynski is instead sparring with a fellow student, a haughty older boy played by the reliable Gus Halper, who did towering work as another collegiate monster in the under-seen 2016 frat-hazing thriller Goat . Had Tremblay and Crowe been given more opportunity to go toe to toe, something in the picture might have caught flame. Instead, Unabomber trudges through its motions, toggling between grim school daze and a tediously generic FBI manhunt. In the latter part, Shailene Woodley does her best to give some texture to her rogue agent character, Joanne, but she has precious little to work with. Perhaps cognizant of that, the filmmakers give Joanne a brief, humanizing button at the end of the film, a moment of solitude in which she has a cathartic cry as she processes all that she’s just experienced. The scene might register as thoughtful were it not such a blatant rip-off of the closing seconds of Zero Dark Thirty , in which a dogged investigator who’s finally caught her prey sheds tears of relief and exhaustion and something more ineffable. It doesn’t pack the same punch the second time around, and at the end of something so bland. Watching Unabomber , one longs for a smarter, more sophisticated, more probing version of this same double-act. A better film about what might have radicalized Ted Kaczynski that also delineates how he was eventually captured could be startling and revealing, complicating the public idea of Kaczynski as mere renegade madman. But this film serves up only the most basic, obvious version of that — try as it might, at times, to immerse us in murky psychological depths. In the end, it has all the markings of a final paper written by a student who got all the dates right, but failed to find the real meaning behind any of the history. Full credits Release date: Friday, Sept. 25 Cast: Russell Crowe, Jacob Tremblay, Shailene Woodley, Annabelle Wallis, Gus Halper Director: Janus Metz Screenwriters: Sam Chalsen, Nelson Greaves Cinematographer: Yves Bélanger Production designer: Michele Laliberte Costume designer: Veroniqué Marchessault Music: Marco Beltrami Editor: Zach Staenberg Casting: Christine Kromer Rated R, 1 hour 37 minutes THR

title: Streaming Ratings: ‘Reacher’ Tops 1 Billion Viewing Minutes for Fifth Straight Week
full_text: Skip to main content By Rick Porter Plus Icon Rick Porter Television Business Editor rickporter Follow Sign Up View All September 24, 2026 3:13pm Alan Ritchson in 'Reacher' season four. Everett Collection Logo text Prime Video’s Reacher continued its strong season four run into the second week of September, scoring more than a billion minutes of viewing for the fifth consecutive week. The series also repeated as the No. 1 overall streaming title in the United States, according to Nielsen. Reacher , which had 1.18 billion viewing minutes in the week of Sept. 7-13, has held that spot in four of the five weeks since it premiered in mid-August. The Gentlemen improved some in its second week after the premiere of season two, rising 22 percent to 881 million minutes of watch time on Netflix. Hulu’s The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives rejoined the charts with the release of a new season, drawing 561 million viewing minutes. Apple TV’s Silo (418 million minutes) also hung on in the top 10 originals a week after its third season finale. Related Stories TV TV Ratings: '60 Minutes' Is Both Up and Down in Week 2 TV Alan Ritchson Reveals Which 'Reacher' Season Got Canceled After "Someone Got Re-Elected" The Big Bang Theory dipped back below a billion minutes but still finished second overall with 971 million viewing minutes and led the acquired series top 10. Former TNT series Major Crimes debuted in the rankings with 906 million minutes on Netflix and Pluto TV (it was added to Netflix on Sept. 3). Major Crimes is a spinoff of The Closer , which had a six-week run on the charts at the beginning of the year. Lanterns (525 million minutes on HBO Max) improved a little on its chart debut the previous week. Tyler Perry’s Netflix film Why Did I Get Married Again? topped the movie rankings and was third among all titles with 908 million minutes of watch time. The 1998 movie Practical Magic (236 million minutes on HBO Max) hit the charts in the same week its sequel was released in theaters. Nielsen’s streaming ratings cover viewing on TV sets only and don’t include minutes watched on computers or mobile devices. The ratings only measure U.S. audiences. title: SCAD Savannah Film Fest: Directors of 10 of 2026’s Top Documentaries Set for ‘Docs to Watch’ Panel (Exclusive)
full_text: × Skip to main content By Scott Feinberg Plus Icon Scott Feinberg Executive Editor of Awards ScottFeinberg Follow Sign Up View All September 24, 2026 3:07pm (Top row, L to R) 'American Doctor,' 'Avedon,' 'Cookie Queens,' 'Everest: The Other Side' and 'The Last First: Winter K2'; (bottom row, l to r) 'My Undesirable Friends: Part II – Exile,' 'Once Upon a Time in Harlem,' 'One in a Million,' 'The Trial of Alec Baldwin' and 'You Can See Everything.' Ibrahim Al-Otia/Watermelon Pictures/Courtesy Everett Collection; Susan Middleton/Netflix; Roadside Attractions/Courtesy Everett Collection; Jimmy Chin; Apple TV+; Venice Film Festival; Sundance Film Festival (2); Blue Ant; A24 The SCAD Savannah Film Festival and The Hollywood Reporter have announced the 10 standout 2026 documentaries that will be represented by their directors on the 13th annual edition of Docs to Watch, the fest’s panel that has become an important stop on the road to the Oscars for nonfiction films. This year’s selections: Poh Si Teng’s American Doctor (Watermelon), Ron Howard’s Avedon (Netflix), Alysa Nahmias’s Cookie Queens (Roadside), Jimmy Chin and Elizabeth Chai Vasarhelyi’s Everest: The Other Side (Nat Geo), Amir Bar-Lev’s The Last First: Winter K2 (Apple), Julia Loktev’s My Undesirable Friends: Part II – Exile (MUBI), William Greaves and David Greaves’s Once Upon a Time in Harlem (Neon), Itab Azzam & Jack MacInnes’s One in a Million (Frontline), Rory Kennedy’s The Trial of Alec Baldwin (Abramorama) and Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s You Can See Everything (A24). Related Stories Movies A24 Fixes Viral Typo in Elizabeth Holmes Documentary Trailer That Baffled Fans General News Elizabeth Holmes to Be Moved From Prison to Halfway House in 2027 Over the past 12 years, 27 films that were represented on the panel went on to receive an Oscar nomination for best documentary feature, and eight ultimately won that award: 2015’s Amy , 2016’s O.J.: Made in America , 2017’s Icarus , 2018’s Free Solo , 2019’s American Factory , 2021’s Summer of Soul , 2022’s Navalny and 2023’s 20 Days in Mariupol . The 2026 panel will take place over 90 minutes at the Lucas Theatre on the afternoon of Wednesday, Oct. 28, and will be moderated by yours truly. “This year’s Docs to Watch selections reflect a range of films that take us somewhere we didn’t expect to go, whether that’s into a hidden chapter of history, the life of an extraordinary individual, or a story unfolding in front of us right now,” Christina Routhier, the senior executive director of SCAD Theaters and Festivals, said in a statement. “We’re excited to partner with Scott Feinberg and The Hollywood Reporter to bring these filmmakers and their films to Savannah and give our students and audiences the chance to experience the work, meet the artists behind it, and be part of the conversation.” Here are some brief loglines about each of 2026’s Docs to Watch: • American Doctor , a film independently financed and directed by a Malaysian-born American journalist, follows three American physicians — one Jewish, one Palestinian and one Zoroastrian — as they volunteer at a hospital in Gaza amid the ongoing war • Avedon , from Oscar-winning director Ron Howard, explores the life, work and legacy of the American portrait photographer Richard Avedon, drawing upon unprecedented access to his personal archives and including never-before-seen stills and behind-the-lens footage • Cookie Queens , the year’s highest-grossing non-celebrity doc, is a heartwarming chronicle of four young girls’ efforts, in the face of varying forms of adversity, to meet their sales goals during Girl Scouts cookie-selling season • Everest: The Other Side , from the Oscar-winning directors of Free Solo , is another film about extreme outdoor athletes, in this case a man and a woman who fall in love and share a dream of climbing and then skiing down the north face of Mt. Everest • The Last First: Winter K2 follows a team of mountaineers as they strive to achieve something never previously accomplished, namely, climbing K2, the second-highest mountain in the world after Mt. Everest, in winter • My Undesirable Friends: Part II – Exile is the six-hour second installment, following a five-hour first, in an epic portrait of independent Russian journalists whose coverage amid Vladimir Putin’s authoritarian crackdown forces them to flee their homeland • Once Upon a Time in Harlem is a miraculous achievement, featuring remarkable footage of a gathering of Harlem Renaissance luminaries that was shot by one filmmaker in 1972 but not turned into a film until that filmmaker’s son completed it more than a half-century later • One in a Million , the winner of the Sundance Film Festival’s audience award, chronicles a tumultuous decade in the life of a young Syrian girl who, along with her family, flees her war-torn country and seeks refuge in Europe • The Trial of Alec Baldwin is the result of exclusive access to the titular star following a 2021 accidental shooting during the making of the film Rust , and includes powerful footage from the set, from Baldwin’s police interrogation and from the legal proceedings that followed • You Can See Everything , a film unlike any other, follows The Rehearsal ’s Nathan Fielder as he is welcomed into the home of Theranos’ Elizabeth Holmes over the 34 days before begins serving a prison sentence, and tries to figure out what she’s really about The 29th SCAD Savannah Film Festival will take place Oct. 24-31. Presented by the Savannah College of Art and Design, it is the largest university-run film festival in the world. Each year, some 75,000 people attend the eight-day event, which attracts some of the biggest names in Hollywood and world cinema, and which features exclusive screenings, panel discussions and workshops. Tickets for this year’s fest are now on sale . THR

title: Reality Producers Rejoice As Federal Film & TV Incentive Bill Includes Unscripted Series
full_text: Skip to main content By Peter White Peter White Executive Editor, Television @peterzwhite More Stories By Peter ‘American Idol’s Luke Bryan, Lionel Richie, Carrie Underwood & Ryan Seacrest Return For Season 25 Reality Producers Rejoice As Federal Film & TV Incentive Bill Includes Unscripted Series Netflix’s Bela Bajaria Confirms Interest In Men’s Soccer World Cup Rights View All September 24, 2026 3:57pm 'Wonka's The Golden Ticket' is shot in Australia Netflix Unscripted television producers, long used to playing second fiddle to the feature film business and scripted TV world, are “ecstatic” that their trade is also being covered by the federal film and TV incentive that was introduced by lawmakers Thursday morning. This was not an accident; Deadline understands that a group of unscripted producers and associations spent a large part of the summer lobbying for inclusion to stem the wave of big-budget competition shows and reality series that were moving out of the U.S. Related Stories Politics Lawmakers Introduce Bill For 20% Federal Film & TV Incentive — Read The Bill Executives Reality Shows Are Increasingly Shot Abroad, But Networks & Streamers Would Like To Film More In U.S. – Reality TV Summit Deadline spoke to around half a dozen unscripted producers, who were elated about the possibility of shooting more of their shows in the U.S., rather than abroad. Watch on Deadline Yes, Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil was shot in the Czech Republic and Ridley Scott took Jacob Elordi to Italy rather than Colorado for The Dog Stars , but the large proportion of unscripted productions that have decamped to Australia, Canada, Ireland and Portugal over the past few years has been staggering. Netflix ’s Wonka’s The Golden Ticket was shot in Australia and its upcoming take on Monopoly was filmed in the UK; ABC’s upcoming Parker Posey-fronted mystery series The Mob was filmed in Italy, while Fox produces the likes of MasterChef and Fear Factor in Canada and Don’t Forget the Lyrics and Next Level Chef in Ireland. Jay Pharoah, host of Fox game show The Quiz with Balls , told Deadline recently that his show has been shot in Australia and Belgium and he wasn’t a particular fan of the food in the latter. “[President Donald] Trump got into office and there was a lot of different shifts with shooting. My understanding is that it’s easier and cheaper to shoot out of America now, which is ridiculous, but that’s how it is,” he said. Similarly, Rob Lowe said the fact that it’s cheaper to bring 100 people to Ireland to shoot The Floor than film in L.A. was “criminal.” Unfortunately for Pharoah and Lowe, there are some exclusions including for game shows, so the pair are likely to keep traveling to Europe for their paychecks. Unscripted producers have long battled generous incentives in Europe, not helped by Ireland’s introduction of the first tax credit specifically for unscripted shows , and cheaper crews abroad. If the Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act, which was sponsored by Republican Tim Scott and Democrat Adam Schiff in the Senate and a number of House members, passes through Congress as is, it will include unscripted series that consist of at least four episodes with a budget of over $1 million where at least 75% of the production is in the U.S. Deadline understands that NPACT (formed in 2017 through the merger of the Nonfiction Producers Association and PactUS) and its general manager Michelle Van Kempen were integral to the process through conversations with the MPA, Film USA and offices of congressional representatives and senators such as South Carolina’s Scott and California’s Schiff. The association, which represents producers such as Bunim-Murray, Kinetic Content, Lionsgate Alternative TV and Studio Lambert, provided economic data to highlight the nature of the challenge. “This is fantastic for unscripted employment,” one source told Deadline. Shawn Moffat, who runs Media Content Services and Ghost Adventures producer My Entertainment, was also a key figure in these conversations. Moffat had conversations with NPACT and also brought together a group of unscripted producers — including Fulwell Entertainment, which merged with LeBron James’ SpringHill Entertainment, Peyton Manning’s Omaha Productions and Mark Wahlberg’s Unrealistic Ideas — to navigate the process. It’s also not only a bill to help Hollywood, but also for film and TV workers across the country, and the proposed legislation includes a 5% uplift for shooting in rural areas. “Whether you’re in South Carolina or California or New Orleans, if you can be in your in your market and go home to your bed every night and still make good TV, that’s what this should be for,” added another source. It’s unclear why game shows are excluded, alongside news, interview and talk shows, awards programming and live sporting events. Networks and streamers from Netflix to CBS would like to shoot more unscripted shows in the States, and a federal incentive will likely make it easier to make that argument. Allison Wallach, Head of Unscripted Programming at Fox Entertainment Studios, recently told Deadline the company is “absolutely leaning into filming here, if we can.” All of this comes as individual states are fighting to nab productions, such as Georgia becoming the new home of American Idol and potentially America’s Got Talent, while New Jersey is now home to The Masked Singer . California finally opened the door for tax credits for unscripted by including competition shows in AB1138 (though it seems only one show – Mark Rober’s Jimmy Kimmel-produced Netflix series Schooled! – has succeeded so far). That is a separate conversation heating up alongside the federal incentive, all moves that should help an embattled sector feel somewhat optimistic about the next few years. ‘Avengers: Endgame: Encore’ & ‘Primetime’ Eye $3M Previews ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Creators On ‘Big Bang’, Meta Finale & Season 2 Judge Grants Suit Settlement Delay; Company Proceeds With $7.5B Debt Raise David Ellison Dines With Trump & Xi; WBD’s CNN, MS Now Denied Access To Event Read More About: 6 Comments

Discovery . It began the process after a legal settlement earlier this week paved the way for the merger to close. Discovery and the repayment of certain existing debt,” the company said today. On Monday, it settled an antitrust suit brought by a group of 12 State Attorneys General led by California’s Rob Bonta. Bankers then started reaching out to investors ahead of the sale of what’s said to be $49 billion in total debt financing. Watch on Deadline The judge in the case must approve the settlement. That includes the $7.5 billion of investment-grade loans, which started moving forward today; about $30 billion of investment-grade bonds; and some $12 billion of second-lien bonds. Debt syndication is a collaborative process led by underwriters where a group of lenders pool resources to fund a large loan for one borrower – in this case Paramount. title: Dealmakers React To Paramount-WBD Settlement: “Tech Has Won”
full_text: Skip to main content By Dade Hayes Dade Hayes Business Editor @dadehayes More Stories By Dade As Letterboxd Draws Interest From The New York Times, A24 And More, One Of Its Bankers Calls It “A Phenomenon” Barry Diller Drops $18B Bid To Acquire Full Control Of MGM Resorts As YouTube Remains Streaming’s Alpha Dog, It’s Adding Even More Unlikely New TV Tricks View All September 24, 2026 11:24am Story Arc Getty Images Mergers-and-acquisitions specialists weighed in Thursday on the Paramount -Warner Bros. Discovery merger, which appears just days from closing despite an 11th-hour legal hiccup. The $110 billion deal is on track to close in the coming days after a settlement of two antitrust lawsuits on Monday, though a federal judge delayed a hearing where she was due to review the settlement. Assuming it does finally close, the transaction “is evidence that, really, tech has won,” said David Hernand, a partner at the Simpson Thacher law firm, during a panel at the Financial Times Business of Entertainment Summit. “Tech came in and said, ‘We can build a better mousetrap on the distribution side.’ Distribution – when we’re talking about electronic distribution, whether it’s cable or internet – is moving atoms, and tech companies are really good at that, as it turns out.” Related Stories News Paramount Moves Ahead With $7.5 Billion Debt Raise, Part Of Package To Finance WBD Acquisition Legal ParaBros Merger Settlement Sign-Off Delayed As Deal Foes Granted Hail Mary Move By Judge Forced to go up against Apple, YouTube, Netflix, Amazon and others, Hernand added, “the traditional companies that relied on broadcast and cable as a form of distribution are trying to play catch-up and figure out how they’re going to play in this world.” Watch on Deadline Hernand’s firm is not involved in the Paramount deal, but two other panelists spoke from the perspective of stakeholders in the transaction. Aaron Sobel, a private equity partner at Apollo Global Management, which provided one-third of the financing for the merger, said it will give a traditional player a fighting chance against Big Tech. “I don’t think you can overstate how important getting that deal done was,” he said. “You had two companies that arguably couldn’t have existed without combining, and having someone like [Paramount CEO David Ellison] support the business is huge.” Prior to the merger, he added, “We were at a crossroads in the industry, where if that deal hadn’t gotten done … Netflix was gonna take over the world. Now, you’re seeing the pendulum really swing back to more traditional media, which is kind of ironic. And David is really betting on IP and what’s in that complex. So the fact that he’s the right owner for that and has the capital, obviously, to support that company, I don’t think you can overstate it.” Alex Michael, senior managing director and global head of sports and entertainment for LionTree, which advised Paramount on the merger, called it “a big deal, literally and figuratively… It was a big domino that everyone was waiting for, and I think it’ll be exciting to see where we go from here.” Sobel said the merger will have “so-many knock-on effects” in a positive way, across the theatrical movie business, distribution, production and “global movies and events.” Noting Hernand’s point, he said the deal was “against where the world was going. And I think there’s a lot of really exciting things that will come out of it.” Netflix, whose chief content officer, Bela Bajaria, spoke just prior to the panel, was the next topic. The streaming giant had agreed to acquire the studio and streaming business of WBD last December. After more than a dozen offers, Paramount finally managed to unseat Netflix with a richer offer for all of WBD. Netflix “kind of showed their hand by going after Warner Brothers, and with all due respect, look at their share price performance,” Sobel said. “The world knows what’s happening on engagement. If you don’t have really valuable IP, they’re going to shift to more traditional strategy over the next few years,” particularly with live events and sports. Noting that “what’s old is new again” for all players in media and entertainment, whether traditional or tech, he added, “I think a lot more of these companies are gonna look similar, not different.” Paramount-WBD is far from the last transaction set to reshape the industry. The panel wrapped with a provocative audience question from an NBCUniversal exec who asked the panel what the best path forward for her company would be. Comcast over the summer announced it plans to spin off NBCU, projecting the move will be completed by mid-2027. Hernand said the company should consider breaking up the portfolio “beyond what they’ve announced, meaning potentially separating NBC from Universal. “The more interesting move there would be combining Universal and Sony,” he added, acknowledging, “I know that would create a lot of outrage in Los Angeles.” Sobel noted that Comcast Co-CEO and Chairman Brian Roberts and his family control the company, and so-called “controlled companies” are often limited in terms of M&A. If Roberts is “open to be more flexible on how his vote works and his exposure to the business, it should be broken up,” Sobel said. “I would think Netflix and Comcast down the digital and the media side should probably come together at some point.” ‘Avengers: Endgame: Encore’ & ‘Primetime’ Eye $3M Previews ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Creators On ‘Big Bang’, Meta Finale & Season 2 Judge Grants Suit Settlement Delay; Company Proceeds With $7.5B Debt Raise David Ellison Dines With Trump & Xi; WBD’s CNN, MS Now Denied Access To Event More from this Story Arc Paramount WB September 24, 2026 David Ellison Dines With Trump & Xi As CEO’s Soon-To-Be Owned CNN Banned From White House Event September 24, 2026 No ParaBros Decision Today As Judge Delays Settlement Sign-Off; CA AG’s Office Insists Deal “Not The Result Of Collusion” View All Story Arc Read More About: Comments

title: $111 billion me…
full_text: Skip to main content By Jill Goldsmith Jill Goldsmith Co-Business Editor More Stories By Jill Paramount Moves Ahead With $7.5 Billion Debt Raise, Part Of Package To Finance WBD Acquisition Kunhardts Expand Life Stories Platform With Unseen Footage From Decades Of Documentary Filmmaking Ex-Disney CEO Bob Chapek Blames Bob Iger For Ouster In New Memoir View All February 27, 2026 1:37pm Story Arc David Ellison Eamonn M. McCormack/Getty Images for Paramount Pictures It’s official. For real this time. Warner Bros. Discovery is selling itself to Paramount for $31 a share in cash in a deal worth $110 billion. The companies unveiled their formal agreement on Friday. Paramount will hold a conference call and webcast on Monday at 8:30am ET to discuss the deal. Related Stories News David Zaslav Tries To Sell Paramount Deal To Shocked & Disappointed Employees At Town Hall: “We’re The Envy Of All Of The Industry” Executives Is Paramount’s Debt-Laden WBD Takeover Another Ill-Starred Hollywood Sequel? The formal announcement comes after WBD jilted Netflix, saying it received a Superior Proposal from the David Ellison company. Netflix had four days to match but declined immediately and walked away, leaving Par triumphant after a months-long hostile takeover attempt to pry apart its rivals. Paramount said the merged company is committed to producing a minimum of 30 theatrical films annually — 15 per studio per year. It promised film will receive a full theatrical release, with a minimum 45-day window globally and the current industry standard home video window prior to availability on subscription streaming services. Doubts around Netflix’s ultimate commitment to theatrical and intermediate windows was a major concern fo exhibitors and many in the Hollywood community. Watch on Deadline The merger is expected to close in the third quarter of 2026, subject regulatory clearances and approval by WBD shareholders, with a vote expected in the early spring. Paramount expects over $6 billion in cost synergies, short for cost savings. It cited a “combination of: technology integration (such as migrating the combined company to a single enterprise resource planning system and consolidating streaming technology stacks), corporate-wide efficiencies, including procurement savings, optimizing the combined real estate footprint, and otherwise streamlining operational efficiencies.” Many industry players anticipate thousands of layoffs. The transaction is funded by $47 billion in equity fully backed by the Ellison Family and RedBird Capital Partners. At closing, the equity may include other strategic and financial partners. Paramount did not name them but its previous hostile tender offer included backing from the Public Investment Fund (Kingdom of Saudi Arabia), L’imad Holding Company PJSC (Abu Dhabi) and Qatar Investment Authority (Qatar). Affinity Partners, the investment fund of President Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner , had also been involved but withdrew. Ditto for China’s Tencent. Under the terms of the equity commitments, new shares of Class B Paramount stock will be issued at a price of $16.02 per share. In addition to the new cash equity investment, the transaction is backed by $54 billion of debt commitments from Bank of America, Citigroup, and Apollo, which includes $15 billion to backstop WBD’s existing bridge facility and $39 billion of incremental new debt. The $54 billion excludes $3.5 billion of bridge financing from these institutions to backstop an existing $3.5 billion revolving credit facility. The combined company will own a film library of more than 15,000 titles and thousands of hours of television programming with franchises including Harry Potter , Mission Impossible , Lord of the Rings, Game of Thrones, the DC Universe, Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles , Transformers, Star Trek and SpongeBob SquarePants . Combined sports rights will include the NFL, Olympics, UFC, PGA Tour, NHL, Big Ten and Big 12 Football, NCAA College Basketball, and Champions League, with the ability to distribute these rights collectively across all of its platforms. The merged company will have a massive portfolio of cable networks. That will include CNN, to the alarm of some lawmakers and many in the news business given shifts at CBS since David Ellison acquired control. The new company will inherit a diverse international portfolio from the former Discovery Communications, present in over 200 countries and territories with cable and free-to-air networks. Ellison, the son of Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison, has stressed technology and today’s announcement promised streamlining of “the technological underpinning of every aspect of the combined company’s businesses.” Paramount said it will be well-positioned to invest in growth, noting marquee deals since the Skydance merger with Trey Parker and Matt Stone of South Park , the UFC, the Duffer Brothers and Activision. However, Wall Streeters have noted it will carry a huge amount of debt that may constrain investment. “From the very beginning, our pursuit of Warner Bros. Discovery has been guided by a clear purpose: to honor the legacy of two iconic companies while accelerating our vision of building a next-generation media and entertainment company. By bringing together these world-class studios, our complementary streaming platforms, and the extraordinary talent behind them, we will create even greater value for audiences, partners and shareholders — and we couldn’t be more excited for what’s ahead,” said Paramount CEO David Ellison. “I’m very pleased with the outcome we achieved for WBD shareholders and the entertainment industry. Our guiding principle throughout this process has been to secure a transaction that maximizes the value of our iconic assets and our century-old studio while delivering as much certainty as possible for our investors. title: Striving to get a settlement
full_text: Skip to main content By Dominic Patten Dominic Patten Executive Editor, Legal, Labor & Politics @DeadlineDominic More Stories By Dominic Disney Legal Chief Warns Of “Hard Choices” & “Much Smaller Organization” Coming As Company Layoffs Loom David Ellison Dines With Trump & Xi As CEO’s Soon-To-Be Owned CNN Banned From White House Event No ParaBros Decision Today As Judge Delays Settlement Sign-Off; CA AG’s Office Insists Deal “Not The Result Of Collusion” View All September 24, 2026 12:12pm Story Arc L-R: Rob Bonta, Leticia James and David Ellison Getty Images Although David Ellison has given a lot of money to Democrats over the years, the Paramount CEO is probably not donating a dime to Sen. Cory Booker ‘s next campaign. The much disparaged state Attorneys General-negotiated settlement in Paramount’s $111 billion acquisition of Warner Bros Discovery did not receive the court approval Thursday for which Rob Bonta and Ellison had hoped. Related Stories News Cory Booker Slams Paramount-WBD Merger Settlement But Blames Company And DOJ, Not State AGs News Block The Merger Coalition Asks Judge To Give Them Time To Formally Oppose Settlement Of Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery Merger Lawsuit Instead, with briefs expected by midnight tonight from opponents of the mega-merger and Paramount moving ahead with a $7.5 billon debt raise, Judge Araceli Martinez-Olguin told the assembled attorneys in a hearing today that she wanted them to address by September 29 concerns raised against the deal earlier Wednesday by longtime merger foe Booker (D-NJ). Stressing “I’ll get you a ruling in due course” (and probably stressing out Ellison as a $7 million-a-day ticking fee looms beginning October 1), the U.S. District judge also had some questions today – a lot of questions. Watch on Deadline Addressing a screen full of top firm lawyers and state AG officials during the virtual hearing, Martinez-Olguin wanted to know if the settlement and the consent decree actually “addresses the Clayton Act concerns” that were in the July 13 antitrust suit Bonta, New York’s Letitia James, and 10 other blue-state AGs filed against the merger. With the sharp realpolitiks at play from California Gov. Gavin Newsom and others for a settlement, Martinez-Olguin also had concerns that the roller-coaster deal was “not the result of collusion and was more of an arm’s length process.” Her blunt words clearly landed hard with her immediate audience of attorneys (and maybe the more than 640 others on the Zoom). Even before the judge issued her “homework” for the lawyers, the California Senior Assistant AG Paula Blizzard argued for the settlement while at the same time dismissing Paramount’s “threats” and “blackmail” to “pull out of California.” However, claiming the states were still prepared to take the whole matter to trial starting March 2, 2027 if the consent degree wasn’t approved, Blizzard also acknowledged the backlash the settlement has received over the past 72 hours since it was unveiled on Monday morning. “We absolutely recognize that this merger has engendered a large amount of controversy and commentary and feelings and concerns on a whole host of issues,” she said near the end of the nearly one-hour session. “A lot of these are outside antitrust,” Blizzard added. “They reflect the country’s very broad political and philosophical divides, concerns about the state of the news media, people’s relationship to big companies and consolidation and corporate power, and we hear those voices, we listen to those voices, we respect those voices. But at the end of the day, this is an antitrust case, and it is focused on the antitrust law.” Sen. Cory Booker Photo by Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images Booker’s six-page letter to the judge Wednesday asked for her to “subject the proposed consent decree to an independent public-interest review before entering it.” Paramount filed paperwork of its own Wednesday, just before the virtual hearing, essentially telling the Garden State senator to mind his own business. During today’s hearing, Blizzard appeared to address Booker’s concerns without saying his name. Insisted the deal was “presumptively valid,” she told Martinez-Olguin it was the result of a final surge of talks over “tens of hours, in-person video conferences, phone conferences, drafts-all the normal things you would see in a consent decree, except magnified because you had 12 attorneys general on our side.” It should be noted, New Jersey was one of the states in the ParaBros antitrust gang, and their AG Jennifer Davenport agreed to the settlement announced September 21. The iconic gates of Paramount Pictures Mark Davis/Getty Images Aware his bosses were watching, Paramount outside counsel Josh Holiann made a point of disputing the use of the term ” blackmail” when it came to timed leaks the Ellisons were serious about pulling up Melrose lot stakes, jobs and productions to redder jurisdictions (“It was a business decision …Paramount had to make.”). In a less defensive posture, the Latham & Watkins attorney also promised the judge the penalties in the settlement would now “keep our feet to the fire.” Still, With Para and WBD lawyers Holian, Beth Wilkinson, Jeffrey Kessler, Daniel Petrocelli and Marguerite Sullivan on-screen (some clearly working on something else), it was mainly Blizzard who took point trying to sell Martinez-Olguin on the deal — and it sure seemed like a hard sell. “We believe we have five years of remedies that will remove the competitive concerns we see the harms we see and preserve competition,” Blizzard said. With nodded agreement from Paramount attorneys, Blizzard stressed the divestment of some cable channels if necessary and Miramax and other clauses in the settlement is “the best solution” other than blocking “it completely?” Sounding very much like she was arguing for Paramount, Blizzard ventured into some hard Hollywood realities to give the deal context. “Obviously, in this case, Warner Bros originally said it was going to sell its assets,” Blizzard said. “So, if we block this merger, there will probably be another one, perhaps before Your Honor, in a year or so, and is that the best solution for the markets to preserve the competition that the Clayton Act requested.” Kneecapped to some extent by Zoom-wide technical glitches that initially prevented some of the attorneys and state government officials from participating in the virtual hearing, the hearing on the now delayed settlement sign-off was delayed itself by nearly 15 minutes. Now, with that ticking fee clock ticking, ParaBros closure is also once again delayed — at least until Monday at noon. Well played Sen. title: David Ellison Dines With Trump & Xi As CEO’s Soon-To-Be Owned CNN Banned From White House, Again
full_text: Skip to main content By Dominic Patten Dominic Patten Executive Editor, Legal, Labor & Politics @DeadlineDominic More Stories By Dominic ParaBros Foes Urge Court To Reject Settlement In Midnight Filings: “This Merger Lessens Competition” Disney Legal Chief Warns Of “Hard Choices” & “Much Smaller Organization” Coming As Company Layoffs Loom No ParaBros Decision Today As Judge Delays Settlement Sign-Off; CA AG’s Office Insists Deal “Not The Result Of Collusion” View All September 24, 2026 5:17pm Story Arc Donald Trump and Melania Trump greet China's Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan to the White House Getty Reporters from CNN aren’t allowed access to the White House’s state dinner or guest arrivals Thursday, but the news outlet’s soon-to-be owner will be breaking bread with China’s president Xi Jinping and Donald Trump , along with a gaggle of tech bosses. Striving to get a settlement in Paramount ‘s $111 billion merger with Warner Bros Discovery approved by a federal judge, CEO David Ellison is among the invited guests to tonight’s superpower sit-down. A past donor to Democrats, the son of Oracle founder and close Trump ally Larry Ellison has become close to the MAGA administration in his pursuit of Paramount last year and more recently WBD. That closeness to Trump has proved a major concern to opponents of the ParaBros mega-deal, especially when it comes to the Bari Weiss-run CBS News and, down the line, CNN . Related Stories News CNN Says It Was Denied Trump White House Access To Cover Arrivals At State Dinner For Chinese President Xi Jinping Legal No ParaBros Decision Today As Judge Delays Settlement Sign-Off; CA AG’s Office Insists Deal “Not The Result Of Collusion” From left: Elon Musk , Mark Zuckerberg, Jeff Bezos and Sam Altman Getty Images The tech-leaning Ellison will be among a band of brothers with Elon Musk, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg, Google co-founder Sergey Brin, TikTok’s Jeff Yass, Nvidia’s Jensen Huang and Microsoft’s Satya Nadella at tonight’s White House event. Along with the titans of traditional industry Trump loves to surround himself with like Boeing CEO Kelly Ortberg, JPMorgan’s Jamie Dimon and Dell’s Michael Dell, Apple’s former CEO Tim Cook and Amazon founder and Washington Post owner Jeff Bezos will be partaking of the three-course meal. Watch on Deadline Chinese officials, White House senior staff, Cabinet members, Trump offspring, congressional GOP leaders and several members of the Supreme Court also are in attendance. Equally unsurprisingly, Fox News ‘ Jesse Watters, Laura Ingraham (called an “American television presenter”) and Bret Baier are on the state dinner guest list with their respective spouses. Banned from the White House by Trump last week, CNN, MS Now and Politico took the administration to court , where Judge Timothy Kelly ordered the outlets be re-credentialed — which they were for a while today and then tonight they were not.

title: CNN & MS Now Say They Were Denied White House Access To Cover Trump’s State Dinner For Chinese President Xi Jinping
full_text: Skip to main content By Ted Johnson Ted Johnson Political Editor @tedstew More Stories By Ted CNN & MS Now Say They Were Denied White House Access To Cover Trump’s State Dinner For Chinese President Xi Jinping Judge Tosses Donald Trump’s Lawsuit Against Des Moines Register And Pollster Ann Selzer Lawmakers Introduce Bill For 20% Federal Film & TV Incentive — Read The Bill View All September 24, 2026 5:27pm U.S. Marines stand guard as they await the arrival of guests for a state dinner where U.S. President Donald Trump hosts Chinese President Xi Jinping in the East Room of the White House. Photo by Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images UPDATED with White House response: Shortly after CNN said that it was denied access to cover the arrivals at the White House State Dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping tonight, MS NOW announced that it, too, had been barred. The news came on the same day a federal judge ordered the White House to restore hard passes to the networks’ journalists and those of and Politico. Related Stories News CNN, MS NOW And Politico Reporters Allowed Back Into White House After Judge’s Order Sidelining Trump Ban News Reporters Committee And Dozens Of Media Outlets File Legal Brief Urging Judge To End Trump’s Ban On CNN, Politico And MS Now The coverage at the North Portico was scheduled to be open to pre-credentialed media, a wider scope of reporters and photographers than the White House press pool. CNN White House correspondent Kristen Holmes said that they were told that their credential to cover the event was only for a camera and audio, not an editorial presence. She had requested that she and her producer attend. Watch on Deadline “Again, no editorial presence, just a camera and audio, which certainly seems like a reaction to President Trump saying that he wanted the CNN coverage of the event,” Holmes said. The White House said on its rapid response account that it was a “pre-credentialed event,” and “contrary to what the fake news wants you the believe, they don’t just get to have free rein into every part of the White House, every event, and every press call.” The exclusion came after U.S. District Judge Timothy Kelly ordered that credentials for CNN, Politico and MS NOW be restored, ending Trump’s five-day ban of the outlets from the White House grounds. The outlets returned to the White House around noon. Then, hours later, Trump complained that CNN and MS NOW were not covering the state visit. Trump claimed that the networks “refused to cover one of the Biggest and Most Beautiful Events to take place in many years, the arrival at the White House of the Highly Respected President of China, Xi Jinping, and his beautiful wife, Madam Peng. The event was magnificent — Actually made for Television but, because they’re Fake News, and because they knew how good it would be, they didn’t want credit to be given to ‘TRUMP,’ they refused to be there. That’s why they have such poor Ratings. Tonight’s State Dinner at the White House, for President Xi, will be spectacular!” In fact, network correspondents said that they were not able to get access to the White House on Thursday morning. And after the White House pulled CNN from the TV pool on Monday, the other four networks in the pool declined to replace them in the rotation. That has meant a dearth of video images from the White House, as TV pool coverage has yet to resume. The latest exclusion does not appear to be addressed in Kelly’s order. Rather, it is an issue about access to a particular event on White House grounds. The press office sends out notice to reporters of events that are open to “pre-credentialed media,” accommodating a much wider scope of credentialed reporters than those restricted to the White House pool. Those who want to attend RSVP, and the White House staff then inform reporters and photographers if they have clearance to go. Last year, after Trump barred the Associated Press from pool access to areas like the Oval Office as well as larger “pre-credentialed media” events in locations like the East Room, the news organization sued. In an initial ruling on a preliminary injunction, a federal judge sided with the AP, concluding that the White House could not bar outlets from press events based on viewpoint. The D.C. Circuit, though, concluded that the White House could exclude the AP from smaller spaces, like the Oval Office and Cabinet Room, but distinguished those areas from larger White House locations like the East Room, where the district judge’s order remains in effect. ‘Avengers: Endgame: Encore’ & ‘Primetime’ Eye $3M Previews ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Creators On ‘Big Bang’, Meta Finale & Season 2 Judge Grants Suit Settlement Delay; Company Proceeds With $7.5B Debt Raise David Ellison Dines With Trump & Xi; WBD’s CNN, MS Now Denied Access To Event Read More About: 5 Comments

title: 'Stuart Fails' Creators On 'Big Bang' OG Return For WGA Strike Roast In Magic-Themed Episode 3…
full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Creators On Magic Of Returning To ‘Big Bang’ Stage, Going Multi-Cam In Meta Season 1 Finale & Season 2 Plans ‘The Beast In Me’ Renewed For Season 2 With Claire Danes Reprising Role; Howard Gordon Back With Netflix Overall Deal David Oyelowo & Viola Prettejohn To Star In ‘The Girl With The Dragon Tattoo’ TV Series For Sky View All August 6, 2026 6:30pm Story Arc (L-R): Kripke (John Ross Bowie) and Stuart (Kevin Sussman) visit 'Big Bang's Bernadette in Episode 3 of 'Stuart Fails To Save the Universe' HBO Max SPOILER ALERT: The story includes details about Episode 3 of HBO Max’s Stuart Fails To Save the Universe . Another episode of Stuart Fails To Save the Universe , another surprise — and dark — OG return. In Episode 3, it was Melissa Rauch reprising her role as Bernadette Rostenkowski. Like in Episode 2, where Penny, in an alternate universe, is with her former boyfriend Zack with no trace of her Big Bang husband Leonard, Bernadette does not have Howard’s last name and appears very much single. She is the focal point of a scene that skewers the 2023 WGA strike with “inside jokes that will be amusing to only 4,000 people in the world,” said Zak Penn , co-creator of the spinoff alongside Big Bang creators Chuck Lorre and Bill Prady . Related Stories Agencies Ari Emanuel On His New Memoir, Nikki Finke, Talking To Trump, AI's Upside & The Hollywood Exec He Hates The Most News 'Stuart Fails To Save The Universe' Creators Wanted Green Lantern For Their DC Crossover Episode But Had To Settle For The Flash The Episode 3 world is ruled by magic , so, to fix their broken alternate reality-hopping machine, Stuart (Kevin Sussman) and Kripke (John Ross Bowie) seek out Bernadette, a renowned local sorcerer. Turns out she is “all out of abracadabra.” What happened? “The Wizards Guild of America claimed I used my powers while we were on strike,” she explained. “What were you on stwike for?,” Kripke asked in his signature speech pattern where “r”s and “l” are replaced by “w”s. “Better dental, residuals for eternal spells. It’s ridiculous, we were out for six months, and basically everyone got a handful of magic beans,” Bernadette said. (You can watch the entire scene below.) For the uninitiated, the Wizards Guild of America shares the same moniker, WGA, with the Writers Guild of America, which Stuart Fails to Save the Universe creators are all members of. The 2023 WGA strike lasted five months with a minimum wage increase, viewership-based streaming residuals and AI protections among the gains in the new agreement with the studios. Melissa Rauch in Episode 3 of ‘Stuart Fails To Save the Universe’ HBO Max Bernadette tells Stuart and Kripke that she was expelled from the guild for using her powers during the strike to bring her neighbor’s son’s adorable rescue dog Chocolate Chip back to life after he was hit by several cars. “I don’t see how that’s bweaking a stwike,” Kripke said. “Exactly,” Bernadette said, adding, “Let me tell you something about Wizards Guild of America. 90% of them don’t even work, and yet they get to vote.” While the percentage is not that high, non-working writers are the majority, representing more than 50% of the full WGA membership that gets to vote to authorize a strike and then to ratify a deal. That has been an ongoing gripe for some established writers and a cause of divide within the union. There was some difference of opinions among the Stuart Fails To Save the Universe creators too during a lively — and funny — interview with Deadline about the WGA strike jabs, which you can (and should) watch below. WGA members caught performing writing services during the strike get expelled, which happened again in 2023. Claiming that an appeal is not an option, Bernadette floats a reversal spell that would give her her powers back that requires “blood of an innocent,” which Stuart qualifies for and provides. Later in the episode, Big Bang ‘s Wil Wheaton shows up to reveal to Stuart that Bernadette is in fact a demon and is killed by Bert (Posehn) in a magic power duel. The episode ends with Bernadette, in a full-on demon form, terrorizing Pasadena and hunting for Stuart & Co. Lorre, Prady and Penn all participated in the 2023 strike and were on the picket lines. Penn has been the most active and public in his pro-WGA stance, having previously served on the WGA West Board of Directors and the union’s Negotiating Committee. (L-R): Bill Prady & Chuck Lorre during the 2023 WGA strike in front of a ‘Big Bang’ banner outside the Warner Bros. TV lot. Bill Prady’s X account DEADLINE: This seemed to me like I could hear Chuck’s voice, all the stuff about Wizards Guild of America. Chuck, you write that speech? And is this what you really think about this writers strike? LORRE : (laughing). PRADY : Oh, this is the Wizards Guild of America, an entirely different organization of wizards. LORRE : Of wizards, yes. The wizards are striking for all the good reasons, and strike breaking is… PRADY : It’s possible that section may include some inside jokes that will be amusing to only 4,000 people in the world. PENN : Also, we have different opinions on this issue, I’d like to say. There’s a continuum of opinions about those issues, but the joke, it can’t be pro-WGA and still be funny. Although let me point out, the WGA rep is right because she is a demon. PRADY : That’s right, Zak is right. The Wizards Guild of America is entirely correct in this episode. LORRE : She broke the strike by bringing Chocolate Chip back to life. PRADY : That’s a lie, that whole chocolate chip story is a lie. PENN : Yeah, she’s a demon. PRADY : She’s a demon. LORRE : Well, yes, but she was also using her powers, and she was supposed to not use her powers during the strike, right? PRADY : Well, we have a different understanding of the episode. I think that entire story is made up. LORRE : Oh, I don’t. PRADY : She makes up that story to get them to give her the blood. I think she made up the whole thing. PENN : You’re getting a little taste of the writers room. With her Demonic transformation, Rauch added a whole new shade of dark to Big Bang alums’ returns for the spinoff, following Kaley Cuoco’s ruthless Penny in Episode 2 and Kunal Nayyar’s deeply depressed Raj in Episode 1. The series’ creators spoke about Big Bang OGs relishing going dark in the spinoff. “Beyond,” Prady said. Added Lorre, “Beyond. It was fun to do something different, that was part of the promise, come and play with us, and we’ll make sure that you’re playing a version of your character you never got to play before, an entirely different approach to the character, and that was fun for the actors.” ‘Avengers: Endgame: Encore’ & ‘Primetime’ Eye $3M Previews ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Creators On ‘Big Bang’, Meta Finale & Season 2 Judge Grants Suit Settlement Delay; Company Proceeds With $7.5B Debt Raise David Ellison Dines With Trump & Xi; WBD’s CNN, MS Now Denied Access To Event More from this Story Arc Stuart Fails To Save The Universe September 24, 2026 ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Creators On Magic Of Returning To ‘Big Bang’ Stage, Going Multi-Cam In Meta Season 1 Finale & Season 2 Plans August 28, 2026 ‘Stuart Fails’ Stars Kevin Sussman & Lauren Lapkus Reveal Filming Episode 6 Scene “Was Terrifying” View All Story Arc Read More About: Comments

title: ‘Stuart’ Episode 3: Wil Wheaton, Brian Posehn & John Ross Bowie Talk Wizards, Puppies, Penguins…
full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Creators On Magic Of Returning To ‘Big Bang’ Stage, Going Multi-Cam In Meta Season 1 Finale & Season 2 Plans ‘The Beast In Me’ Renewed For Season 2 With Claire Danes Reprising Role; Howard Gordon Back With Netflix Overall Deal Terence Winter To Adapt Jay Stratton’s ‘Out Of The Shadows’ Memoir About Investigating Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena As TV Series View All August 6, 2026 6:30pm Story Arc (L-R): Lauren Lapkus, Kevin Sussman, Brian Posehn and John Ross Bowie in Episode 3 of 'Stuart Fails To Save the Universe' HBO Max SPOILER ALERT: The story includes details about Episode 3 of HBO Max’s Stuart Fails To Save the Universe . Three episodes in, Stuart Fails To Save the Universe has brought back seven actors from the original show in addition to the spinoff’s leading quartet of Stuart (Kevin Sussman), Brian Posehn (Bert), Lauren Lapkus (Denise) and John Ross Bowie (Kripke), and has killed off two OG characters in two different universes. First, it was Kunal Nayyar’s opening episode who was shot dead by Kripke . In Episode 3, it is Wil Wheaton , killed with magic by another Stuart Fails To Save the Universe lead character, Bert. Related Stories News 'Stuart Fails To Save The Universe' Creators Wanted Green Lantern For Their DC Crossover Episode But Had To Settle For The Flash News 'Stuart Fails' Stars Kevin Sussman & Lauren Lapkus Reveal Filming Episode 6 Scene "Was Terrifying" Set in a world where magic is real and where, per the opening credits spoiler, “Bert is magic,” Wheaton is a representative of the Wizards Guild of America. He comes after Stuart for unwittingly enabling Bernadette (Melissa Rauch) to resume her demon form after she had been expelled from the guild and stripped of her magic powers. (You can read about Rauch’s return and Bernadette’s beef with the WGA here .) Bert shields Stuart from Wil’s deadly fireball, which leads to a magic fight to the death between the two that destroys most of the comic book shop and ends with Wil’s demise. (You can watch most of the scene below.) “I remember when the script was sent to me, and I was reading through it and not getting most of it because I hadn’t seen anything else,” Wheaton told Deadline. “We get to the magic shop, and I knew that I was going to be a wizard because I’d had a costume fitting, but I didn’t know anything about what it was going to be. What I see in the script is Wil Wheaton and Bert have an epic fireball fight, and I took a picture of it and I texted that picture to Bill and I just said ‘thank you.'” Wheaton spoke about the logistics of filming the fight, in which the Star Trek: The Next Generation alum also got to flash the Vulcan salute. “We had so much fun. Tom [Mahoney], the visual effects supervisor, and Brian and I really went through blocking and coordinating this entire fight sequence, and it was about like, well, how do you tease the fireball up in your hand, and how do you shape the fireballs in your hand?,” he said. “And for a particular kind of nerd, it’s a really big deal to be a wizard throwing a fireball, and to see that, like, I look so much cooler than I’ve ever looked ever in my entire life.” Wheaton revealed an Easter egg he had asked the show’s costume designer Valerie Klarich to incorporate into his costume — which she did. “The character that I play in Felicia Day’s series, The Guild , is Fawkes, he’s the leader of their rival guild. Felicia and I wrote a comic book together about him, and on the cover, there’s this really cool artwork that is Fawkes in a wizard’s robe with all these glowing runes on it. So Val said, ‘Do you have any requests for your costume?’ And I said, ‘If you could put some runes down the sides of the cloak, that would be really cool.’ And she said, ‘Yeah, we know a 3D printing guy who prints on fabric.’ So I got it.” He shared his reaction to the Fawkes-inspired cloak. “When I saw that, I was just like, there’s this great moment in Almost Famous where Lester Bangs says to the kid, ‘Oh no, they made you feel cool, and you’re not cool, so you’re trapped. They made me feel cool, and I’m not cool, and I was like, ‘This is an entirely fine place to be trapped.'” ‘Bert is magic” Posehn spoke of the cool and dark side of Episode 3 where Bert can do magic but he also is almost burnt at the stake for being a scientist. “People here think science is evil,” Kripke said about the magic-ruled alternate reality, to which Stuart responds in a rare topical comment on the show, “How is this different from our world?” “That was a funny episode, and then also that we play off it, where somebody goes, ‘In this world, science is forbidden,’ and Stuart goes, ‘Isn’t that kind of like our world?’ That joke I loved,” Posehn said. “But getting to be burned at a stake as a metalhead — it wasn’t a bucket list thing but getting to do it was super fun.” Posehn is known for his lifelong love for heavy metal which he has blended with stand-up comedy in his novelty comedy-metal tracks. There was another big draw for him in the episode. “I’m the biggest dog nerd you’re gonna meet, so having magic powers where I could make a puppy just transform out of nowhere — that was so fun to shoot,” he said. In the episode, Bert is asked by his acolytes to manifest life and he does it by conjuring up a puppy. “He was so excited about the dog, it was so cute,” Bowie said. “He was so, so pumped about the doggie they gave him.” Added Posehn, “Every time I had to be joyful when I said ‘Abracadabra puppy,’ it was like the easiest acting job I’d ever done because there was a puppy on my lap. So I’m like, ‘Hehehe, look at him! He’s adorable!’ That was super fun to play.” March of the Penguin In the episode, Bert also takes revenge on Kripke for not helping him when he was at the stake by turning him into a penguin sporting Kripke’s hair. Bowie spoke about the method acting involved in playing a penguin. “I went back to the the time in my life that I was a flightless waterfowl, and really went through a lot of sense memory on that,” he joked. “No, it was incredibly fun because I’ve never done mo-cap, I’ve never had one of those suits with the little buttons on them and the camera right in front of your face.” (L-R): Kevin Sussman, Brian Posehn and John Ross Bowie in Episode 3 of ‘Stuart Fails To Save the Universe’ HBO Max There was some VFX wizardry involved in the transformation but also old-fashion practical special effects. “They built a mock-up of the comic book shop that was proportionally larger, and they put an elastic band around my knees so I had to waddle,” Bowie said. “It was really fun, and then the finished product looks amazing, and I love that he’s a penguin with my hair. I thought that was a really good choice to keep this magnificent coif on the penguin. Yeah, I enjoyed that a lot.” ‘Avengers: Endgame: Encore’ & ‘Primetime’ Eye $3M Previews ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Creators On ‘Big Bang’, Meta Finale & Season 2 Judge Grants Suit Settlement Delay; Company Proceeds With $7.5B Debt Raise David Ellison Dines With Trump & Xi; WBD’s CNN, MS Now Denied Access To Event More from this Story Arc Stuart Fails To Save The Universe September 24, 2026 ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Creators On Magic Of Returning To ‘Big Bang’ Stage, Going Multi-Cam In Meta Season 1 Finale & Season 2 Plans August 28, 2026 ‘Stuart Fails’ Stars Kevin Sussman & Lauren Lapkus Reveal Filming Episode 6 Scene “Was Terrifying” View All Story Arc Read More About: Comments

title: ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Renewed For Season 2 By HBO Max
full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Creators On Magic Of Returning To ‘Big Bang’ Stage, Going Multi-Cam In Meta Season 1 Finale & Season 2 Plans ‘The Beast In Me’ Renewed For Season 2 With Claire Danes Reprising Role; Howard Gordon Back With Netflix Overall Deal Terence Winter To Adapt Jay Stratton’s ‘Out Of The Shadows’ Memoir About Investigating Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena As TV Series View All August 14, 2026 12:07pm Story Arc 'Stuart Fails to Save The Universe' HBO Max Stuart will continue to fail in his efforts to save the universe as HBO Max has renewed The Big Bang Theory spinoff for a second season. From creators Chuck Lorre, Zak Penn, and Bill Prady and Warner Bros. TV, the first season of Stuart Fails To Save the Universe is HBO Max’s second-biggest comedy launch ever globally, per the streamer. Not surprisingly, HBO Max’s biggest launch also was a followup to a hugely popular comedy series, Sex and the City sequel And Just Like That … The achievement comes with an asterisk because HBO Max had not debuted a new original comedy series in almost three years, since Lorre’s Bookie premiered in November 2023. Also, the streamer has had a gradual international rollout over the past five years and was not available in Western Europe until 2024 and in some countries, including the U.K. and Germany, until 2026, skewing global viewership comparisons. Related Stories Cancellations and Renewals 2026 TV Series Renewals Photo Gallery News ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’: Here Is Why Episodes Of ‘Big Bang Theory’ Spinoff Are So Short The renewal comes four episodes into Stuart Fails To Save the Universe ‘ Season 1 run; episodes drop weekly every Thursday. The spinoff lives on HBO Max alongside the mothership series; both are exclusive to the Warner Bros. Discovery platform (in the case of The Big Bang Theory, for streaming only). Watch on Deadline “We’re delighted with how this hilarious, genre-bending show from Chuck, Zak, and Bill has connected with the audience, both devotees of The Big Bang Theory and new fans alike,” said Amy Gravitt, EVP, HBO Programming, Head of HBO & HBO Max Comedy Series. “Along with everyone else, we can’t wait to see the worlds they conjure for these beloved characters next season.” A single-camera, sci-fi take on The Big Bang Theory, the spinoff stars four alums from the hit CBS sitcom. It follows comic book store owner Stuart Bloom (Kevin Sussman) who is tasked with restoring reality after he breaks a device built by Sheldon and Leonard, accidentally bringing about a multiverse Armageddon. Stuart is aided in this quest by his girlfriend Denise (Lauren Lapkus), geologist friend Bert (Brian Posehn), and quantum physicist/all-around pain in the ass Barry Kripke (John Ross Bowie). Along the way, they meet alternate-universe versions of characters we’ve come to know and love from The Big Bang Theory. As the title implies, things don’t go well. Those playing alternate versions of themselves so far have included Big Bang stars Kaley Cuoco, Kunal Nayyar and Mayim Bialik. “Chuck, Zak, and Bill delivered something truly special with Stuart Fails To Save the Universe — a completely original take on one of the most beloved franchises of all time that captures the unique essence that made The Big Bang Theory so special,” said Channing Dungey, Chairman and CEO, Warner Bros. Television Group and WBD US Networks. “It’s been an absolute joy to see audiences embrace this next iteration so passionately, and we can’t wait to continue exploring the multiverse in season two.” The series stars Kevin Sussman (Stuart), Lauren Lapkus (Denise), Brian Posehn (Bert), and John Ross Bowie (Kripke). Stuart Fails To Save the Universe , from Chuck Lorre Productions in association with Warner Bros. Television, is created, written, and executive produced by Big Bang creators Lorre & Prady and Penn. title: ‘Stuart Fails’ Stars Kevin Sussman & Lauren Lapkus Reveal Filming Episode 6 Scene “Was Terrifying&#8221…
